analysis:
The PR changes two files. In EngineV2Factory+BackendPreparation.swift (head line 458), prepareProductionBackend now passes its `environment` into makeSegmentedPagedBackend. The rest of that file is unchanged GLM and paged logic. In EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift, makeSegmentedPagedBackend adds two PagedKVPoolConfig fields, `retainedFreeSegmentBytes` and `hostZeroedSegments`. Retention is on by default and is disabled only by DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION=0. Host zeroing is on while retention is on and is disabled by DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS=0. The retained cap is min(2 GiB, grant/8).

Security-relevant behavior: free KV segments, which held decrypted per-request KV for A-001, can now stay resident in the process across requests instead of being retired on release. The doc comment says admission reuses 'evaluated KV segments' and avoids 'allocating, filling and fencing'. That suggests the per-segment device zero-fill is skipped on reuse.

What this touches: T-028 (residual data in GPU memory) and T-041 (cross-tenant cache and timing channel). Retained memory stays inside the same attested process (TB-007) and uses the same address space as the already-accepted residue. The pool implementation (PagedKVPool and PagedKVBackend segment reuse and zeroing) is not in the supplied evidence, so I could not verify that a request cannot read stale tenant KV from a reused segment (attention-kernel bounds, valid-length masking, page-table isolation). I also could not verify that hostZeroedSegments zeroes at allocation time and not on reuse, or that retained bytes are charged to GlobalKVCacheBudget so they cannot cause over-commit or DoS (T-016, T-029). Retention can also change TTFT timing, which touches the SEC-035 oracle, but that is within the accepted same-account channel.

The env keys are read from the process environment, which is operator-controlled (ADV-001, TB-003). Operator control of its own process is not a new boundary. No secrets, network, or auth surfaces changed. No finding is raised because nothing here shows a concrete regression; the pool implementation needs review to confirm the reuse isolation and budget accounting. I also recommend updating T-028 to state the retention behavior and its kill switch.
